title: Benedict XIII's cipher letters to Francesc Climent, 1399-1416, Arxiu Capitular de Barcelona (catalogue 334)

steps.what: HathiTrust record 100676638 (Puig 1920) tried in curl and the built-in browser: Cloudflare challenge, not solved. archive.org: no copy.

Butllari de Catalunya (Fundació Noguera 2016), IFC 2024 Benedicto XIII volume, Cuella's Bulario IV, Suárez Fernández's Castilian documents, zaguan 2023 paper grepped for cifra/xifra/criptog: no mention of the ACB cipher letters.

Baucells i Reig 1978 (ACB Cisma d'Occident catalogue, PDF from the ACB site): codices and parchments only; the paper part (1,532 pieces) was uncatalogued; archivist Mas's note that Puig took Schism papers home 1920-30 and many were not returned.
Google Books full-view copy of Puig 1920 found (id CuOlkxWnk-EC, Wisconsin). Book pages and PDF were CAPTCHA-walled, but the in-volume search endpoint and signed page-image URLs answered.

In-volume search for cifra/clave/descifr: p. 466 n. 2 says italics mark the deciphered phrases and Puig rebuilt the key 'a fuerza de paciencia' from lines Climent left on docs. 1063, 461, 463; preface p. 2: 'los diez u once escritos con desconocida clave' deciphered. Appendix index lists 14 'Carta cifrada' items, 1399-1416.
Appendix pages of every cipher item fetched and checked for gaps and for what Puig left unread (page-by-page check by a subagent).

Found that Puig p. 475 carries an uncaptioned, sideways photogravure of the last page of XXXV (22 June 1400, doc. 1068), clear Latin alternating with cipher runs, with Puig's text of the same passage beside it; fetched at the maximum 1826 x 2500 px, rotated and deskewed (0.7 deg), lines segmented.

Known-plaintext alignment of two runs against Puig's italics: line 1-2 'cum duce Burgundie' after a dotted-V sign for the King of Aragon, line 8 'et presertim scribe qu...'. Consistent values u = cb (3x), e = delta (4x), s = T (2x), m = t (2x), d = double cross (2x), c/i = o, b = T-bar; one clash.

Attempted a sign-level transcription of the long run (lines 8-16, about 450 letters of known plaintext) at 3-4x with contrast enhancement: delta/d-with-mark/o/a and joined strokes cannot be separated consistently at this resolution; 'quo modo se habet' did not align. Stopped; recorded as blocked (illegible).

Second session. Tried for a sharper image of p. 475: Google Books serves 1826 x 2500 at most (w=4000 and zoom 4-6 give nothing larger); the second Google copy (wP0wAQAAMAAJ) is snippet view; HathiTrust still behind Cloudflare in curl; Claude in Chrome not connected; no other digitised copy found by web search.

Plate re-cut from the page, rotated, deskewed -0.7 deg by maximising the row-profile contrast, 26 line centres found from the smoothed ink profile; each cipher run cut into ~500-750 px strips and viewed at 3-5x with autocontrast, alongside Puig's text of p. 475-476.

Known-plaintext alignment over all cipher runs of the plate (lines 1-6, 8-17, 23-25), word by word against Puig's italics. One sign per letter emerges: a hook, b T-bar, c/i/o o, d double cross, e delta, f flagged sigma, g 4-shape, h 2-shape, l looped d, m footed epsilon, n, p inverted T, q double-barred upright, r upright, s T, t c', u/v cb, x alpha-shape; dotted V = King of Aragon (4x). The first session's clash was a misread of joined strokes.

Word-by-word tally (src/plate475_check.tsv): 148 words, 826 plaintext letters; 125 words confirmed sign by sign, 16 with 1-3 blurred signs, 7 illegible (line 4, underlined/overwritten in the original). 755/826 letters confirmed (91.4%; 96.3% of legible runs); no sign contradicts the key.

The key corrects Puig in three places: 'te sicudum' (line 4) is 'tenendum' (c' delta n delta n dcross cb m-sign; the clear text just before has 'in suspenso tenendum'); 'abique congerio' is 'absque congedio'; 'necesaria' is written 'necessaria'. Four separator groups (lambda/z signs) stand where Puig prints ';' or a dash and are not printed by him: read as null punctuation.

Write-up pass: line 24 (modis ... absque) re-read at 5x and transcribed sign by sign as seen, 58 signs, for the site's decipher replay. It showed that o is a double loop, distinct from the single o used for c and i; one tall stroke in 'istorum' unexplained.

outcome.method_basis: The text is Puig y Puig's printed decipherment (Pedro de Luna, 1920, appendix), found before the attempt; the project then rebuilt Puig's unprinted key by aligning his printed text against the p. 475 facsimile (external plaintext) and confirmed 91.4% of the plate's letters sign by sign.

gaps.item: Fr. Pedro de Vico to Guillem Carbonell, 4 Dec 1398: one cipher line of unknown key (Puig app. XIX, p. 461 n. 3)
gaps.detail: Not printed; the ACB original is not digitised.

gaps.item: Two keys of Climent in doc. 595 that Puig could not apply
P. Jafet to Climent 15 Sep 1400 (doc. 1043) and Comuel to Climent (doc. 661), cited by Puig but not printed
Plate line 4, 'non approbando nec reprobando; de cardinali catan-' (7 words, 42 letters)
gaps.detail: Underlined and overwritten in the original; the halftone does not separate the signs. Needs a photograph of ACB doc. 1068 or a 600-dpi scan of Puig p. 475.

gaps.item: 16 plate words with 1-3 blurred signs (29 letters)
gaps.detail: Listed in src/plate475_check.tsv (status p); nothing contradicts the key.
Read as null punctuation; whether the dotted V inside two of them is meant cannot be settled from four instances.
The key applies, but no image exists; Puig's reading stands for them.

outcome.notes: Read by Puig y Puig in 1920 (the reading is his). Added here: Meister's second-hand ACB report identified with Puig's printed decipherments; the 14 cipher items listed; in a second session the key Puig never printed rebuilt from the p. 475 facsimile against his text (20 letters, name sign, null separators), confirming 91.4% of the plate's cipher letters sign by sign (96.3% of the legible part) with no contradiction, and correcting Puig in three places (tenendum, absque congedio, necessaria). fraction_read is the plate's sign-by-sign confirmed share, not the reading of the text, which is Puig's and complete.

prior.where: Puig y Puig, Pedro de Luna (Barcelona 1920), appendix: deciphered by Puig himself from Climent's partial glosses; not cited by Meister (1906, earlier), Galende 2013, or the cryptologic literature checked.

human: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Opus 5.5 and posed the target with /goal from the archive-scan lead (catalogue 334), naming Puig y Puig 1920 as the outstanding check. No target-specific intervention.
